title: Who knows more?
simplified_paragraphs: 小男孩问爸爸：“是不是爸爸总比孩子知道得多？”
小男孩问：“电灯是谁发明的？”
小男孩又问：“那爱迪生的爸爸怎么没有发明电灯？”爸爸看着他，不知道怎么回答这个问题。
很多时候，我们知道的不一定都是对的，孩子常常能给我们新的启发！
traditional_paragraphs: 小男孩問爸爸：“是不是爸爸總比孩子知道得多？”
小男孩問：“電燈是誰發明的？”
小男孩又問：“那愛迪生的爸爸怎麼沒有發明電燈？”爸爸看著他，不知道怎麼回答這個問題。
很多時候，我們知道的不一定都是對的，孩子常常能給我們新的啟發！
pinyin_paragraphs: xiǎo nán hái wèn bà ba：“ shì bù shì bà ba zǒng bǐ hái zi zhī dào de duō？”
bà ba huí dá：“ dāng rán !”
xiǎo nán hái wèn：“ diàn dēng shì shéi fā míng de？”
bà ba xiào zhe huí dá：“ Ài dí shēng。”
xiǎo nán hái yòu wèn：“ nà Ài dí shēng de bà ba zěn me méi yǒu fā míng diàn dēng？” bà ba kàn zhe tā， bù zhī dào zěn me huí dá zhè ge wèn tí。
hěn duō shí hou， wǒ men zhī dào de bù yī dìng dōu shì duì de， hái zi cháng cháng néng gěi wǒ men xīn de qǐ fā！
english_paragraphs: A little boy asked his dad, “Do dads always know more than their kids?”
The little boy asked, “Who invented the light bulb?”
The little boy asked again, “Then why didn’t Edison’s dad invent the light bulb?” His dad looked at him, unsure how to answer.
Often, what we think we know isn’t necessarily right, and children can give us fresh insights!
english_full:
A little boy asked his dad, “Do dads always know more than their kids?”

“Of course!” his dad replied.

The little boy asked, “Who invented the light bulb?”

His dad smiled and answered, “Edison.”

The little boy asked again, “Then why didn’t Edison’s dad invent the light bulb?” His dad looked at him, unsure how to answer.

Often, what we think we know isn’t necessarily right, and children can give us fresh insights!
